en: The Therāpadāna:
The Chapter on the Lion-Throned One (Sīhāsaniya-vagga), Number Nine: The Apadāna of the Elder Sopāka.
While he was clearing away a mountain slope in a forest on that most excellent of peaks,
the Blessed One named Siddhattha appeared.

He came into my presence. Seeing the Buddha, the Elder of the World, the Neutral One, approaching, I spoke these words: “Welcome, O Blessed One. Then, having paid homage with my head at his feet, I sat down to one side. Seated there, I addressed the Teacher, the Knower of the World, the One Who Has Reached the Further Shore. “O Blessed One, you have come from afar; you have traveled a long distance. May the Blessed One rest for a while. Thus I spoke to the Teacher, the Knower of the World, the One Who Has Reached the Further Shore. “I am rested, O Great King,” he said, “for I have attained the bliss of Nibbāna. May the Blessed One rest for a while. Thus I spoke to the Teacher, the Knower of the World, the One Who Has Reached the Further Shore.
Having spread out a mat,
I offered a seat of flowers.
Having sat down upon that flower-seat,
Siddhattha, the Leader of the World,
having understood my destiny,
proclaimed impermanence.
‘Impermanent indeed are conditioned phenomena,
subject to arising and passing away;
having arisen, they cease.’
“Their pacification is bliss.
Having said this, the All-Knowing One,
the Eldest in the World, the Bull among Men;
The Hero rose up into the sky like a king of swans in the air;
having abandoned his own [wrong] view, he ascended.
I cultivated the perception of impermanence;
having cultivated it for a single day,
I passed away there.
Having experienced two attainments,
impelled by the root of merit,
when his final existence was reached—
I approached the one with the cooked rice.
Having gone forth from the home,
I entered the homeless life.
At seven years of age,
I attained arahantship;
having exerted energy and being resolute in purpose.
Well-composed in the moral precepts,
having pleased the Great Naga,
I received full ordination.
In ninety-four aeons ago,
whatever karma I performed then,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of that gift of flowers.
Because I cultivated mindfulness back then, ninety-four aeons ago;
As I cultivated that perception,
the destruction of the taints was attained by me;
the four analytical knowledges—
And these eight liberations have been attained;
the six direct knowledges have been realized—
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
Thus indeed the venerable elder Sopāka spoke these verses.
This is the ninth legend of the elder Sopāka.
